title: GraphQL: schema, resolvers and the over-fetching problem

videos.script: A phone app opens a book's page, and it needs three things: the book, its author, and the author's other books. With the REST API from lesson 1, that is three requests, one after another. {{rest}} Each answer carries fields the page never shows, and still the page has to come back for more. {{waste}} GraphQL turns this around. There is one address, and the client sends a query that names every field it wants. The answer comes back in exactly that shape. {{query}} In this lesson you write that server for the bookshop. You read its schema, which is the contract, and you watch a resolver run for every field. {{resolvers}} Then you count the SQL it runs. A list of six books costs seven queries, and you bring it down to two. {{count}} You also see what the client's new freedom costs the server. Errors that arrive with a two hundred, a query deep enough to hurt, and caches that stop helping. {{costs}} By the end, you can say when GraphQL is worth it, and when REST is still the better choice. {{choose}}
